title: Reskin lockers
statement: A hotel corridor has $400$ lamps, all off, numbered $1$ to $400$. On day $k$, for $k = 1, 2, \dots, 400$, a caretaker flips the switch of every lamp whose number is a multiple of $k$. How many lamps are on after day $400$?
hints: How many times is lamp $n$ flipped?
Use divisor pairing to find which numbers have an odd number of divisors.
solution: A lamp is flipped once for each divisor of its number, so it ends on exactly when it has an odd number of divisors, that is, when its number is a perfect square. There are $20$ squares up to $400$. Why this works. divisor-pairing: a switch flips once per divisor, and only squares have an odd number.
check_program: print(sum(1 for lamp in range(1, 401) if sum(1 for k in range(1, 401) if lamp % k == 0) % 2 == 1))
